captions.detailed: An external-routing mechanical dropper seatpost assembly consisting of a black outer tube secured at its base by a grey seat-tube binder ring clamp. An inner black post extends upwards from the outer tube, capped with a dual-bolt saddle rail clamp plate that holds a flat-nosed black saddle via two parallel curved steel rails. A side-mounted cable-routing port and a mechanical release cable anchor clamp are mounted on the side of the outer tube. The inner post moves linearly relative to the outer tube via a prismatic joint, while the saddle assembly tilts relative to the inner post on a revolute pivot.
captions.instruction: Create a 3D model of an external-routing mechanical dropper seatpost. It must feature a dark grey seat-tube binder ring clamping the base of a black outer tube, a prismatic joint connecting to an inner post, a side-mounted cable-routing anchor, and a saddle assembly with parallel mounting rails attached to a tilt-adjustable clamp plate.
captions.factory: Construct the outer tube and inner post using concentric cylinders. Model the binder ring clamp at the base using a boolean difference on a thick cylinder to form a split clamp, and add a small screw box. Create the cable routing port and mechanical anchor box on the side of the outer cylinder. Build the saddle clamp plate at the top of the inner tube using a box with holes, and construct the saddle rails using swept profiles or curved cylinders. Finally, model the saddle body using a lofted or extruded flat-nosed shell and define the prismatic joint along the Z-axis and the revolute joint for the saddle tilt.
